question.text: When <math><mtext>A</mtext><mtext>g</mtext><mtext>N</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> solution is added in excess to 1M solution of <math><mtext>C</mtext><mtext>o</mtext><mtext>C</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>l</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mtext>.X</mtext><mtext></mtext><mtext>N</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>H</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> one mole of <math><mtext>A</mtext><mtext>g</mtext><mtext>C</mtext><mtext>l</mtext></math> is formed? What is the value of <math><mtext>'</mtext><mrow><mtext>X</mtext></mrow><mrow><mtext>'</mtext></mrow><mo>?</mo></math> (Assume that the co-ordination number is 6)

solution.text:
CoCl3.XNH3 gives 1 mole of AgCl. So one Cl– ion is outside the complex. So 2Cl– and 4NH3 satisfy coordination number 6.

From the given data the possible complex is

[ Co ( NH 3 ) 4 Cl 2 ]Cl

So x is 4
